💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGGESTION: the scoped wipe is silent — a future no-op would be undiagnosable**

The new wipe only removes a dir when the recorded `WorkspacePath` equals `$(pwd)/ios/Runner.xcworkspace`. That comparison is correct today (the runner's `_work/...` paths are real, non-symlinked), but it is the one failure mode neither the fix nor the guard test can see: if the two spellings of the path ever diverge (a symlinked workspace component, Xcode recording a resolved vs logical path), the wipe **silently no-ops forever** and the gh-1296 failure class (`FlutterPlugin.h has been modified since the module file was built`) returns with nothing pointing at the wipe. `AC3` in the guard test pins the code shape, but cannot detect a runtime no-op.

One echo keeps the protection observable and makes the next stale-pcm red diagnosable in a single read:

```bash
if [ "$ws" = "$ws_path" ]; then
  echo "gh-2134: wiping DerivedData owned by this workspace: $dd"
  rm -rf "$dd"
fi
```

Optionally also emit one line when the loop matched nothing, so "protection ran but found no candidate" vs "protection never matched" is distinguishable in CI logs.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGGESTION: stale `Runner-*` dirs from dead checkouts are now never cleaned**

The old HOME-global glob did two things at once: (a) deleted concurrent builds' live DerivedData — the bug this PR fixes — and (b) garbage-collected stale `Runner-*` dirs whose owning checkout no longer exists. The scoped wipe keeps (a) fixed but drops (b) entirely: a dir whose recorded `WorkspacePath` points at a checkout that is gone (re-registered runner process, renumbered `_work` dir, deleted branch checkout) can now never be removed by any build on the box.

On the shared self-hosted fa-m5 Mac each `Runner-*` dir is multiple GB, so orphans accumulate toward disk exhaustion — and disk pressure produces exactly the `accessing build database ... disk I/O error` class this PR is fixing. Worth a companion sweep so the fix doesn't trade a deterministic race for a slow disk-full drift:

- a scheduled (or pre-build) sweep that removes `Runner-*` dirs whose recorded `WorkspacePath` no longer exists on disk — that condition is race-free by construction (a live leg's checkout always exists);
- or a retention policy (age-based) in the same loop.

Not needed to merge this PR — the correctness of the scoped wipe stands on its own — but the accumulation has no owner otherwise.

## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: Root cause and fix for the gh-2134 build-ios red verified. The HOME-global `rm -rf .../DerivedData/Runner-*` on the shared fa-m5 box (3 concurrent runner processes, one `$HOME`) is now WorkspacePath-scoped via `info.plist` — concurrent legs can never match each other. Verified locally: guard test red on `main` / green on this PR (4/4); wipe loop simulated (matched dir removed; sibling-workspace, plist-less, empty DerivedData all survive, exit 0); `dart format`/`dart analyze` clean; run 43203130726 had exactly one red leg — Build iOS ("Quality gate" is the aggregate check) — so this PR covers the full failure; no other workflow carries the global wipe pattern.

**Key Issues**:
- 💡 `.github/workflows/ci.yml:3225` — the scoped wipe is silent: a future `WorkspacePath` mismatch (symlinked/logical-vs-resolved path) would disable the gh-1296 stale-pcm protection with zero signal; add a one-line echo.
- 💡 `.github/workflows/ci.yml:322` — the scoped wipe no longer garbage-collects stale `Runner-*` dirs from dead checkouts; plan an orphan sweep before disk pressure reproduces the "disk I/O error" class.
- 🪶 digest: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:3213` — wording: the DerivedData dir hash is keyed to the *workspace* path (`Runner.xcworkspace`), not the "checkout path".

**Next Steps**:
1. Optional polish: add the wipe log line (comment 1) — not blocking.
2. Follow-up: orphan `Runner-*` sweep on the fa-m5 box (comment 2) — no owner today.
3. Safe to merge; when the ref goes green, gh-2134 closes per its contract.
